Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:10:2.english: And at the end - When it left the world [i.e., ceased to exist].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:10:4.english: Or drank it - After it increased in value.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:11:1.hebrew: דאי איתה - כאן בשעת התביעה הוה מהדרנא בעינא, דכי אמרינן משלם כשעת הגזילה, היכא דליתה בעין, אבל ישנה בעין, בין שהוקרה בין שהוזלה, חוזרת כמות שהיא. הלכך, הואיל ואם תבעה בעודה קיימת לאחר שהוקרה היתה חוזרת בעין, אשתכח דההיא שעתא דקא שתי לה הוא דגזיל לה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:11:1.english: That if it were [intact] - Here, at the time of the claim, I would return [it] intact; for when we say [that] he pays according to the time of the robbery, [that is] where it is not intact, whereas [if] it is intact, whether it appreciated or depreciated, it returns as it is. Therefore, since if [the owner] had claimed it while it still existed after it appreciated it would have returned intact, it turns out that it is at that moment when he drinks it that he steals it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:13:1.english: And with regard to what - Regarding which [case] do Beit Hillel disagree?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:13:2.hebrew: אי בחסר - כשהוזלה, דקאמרי ב"ש ילקה לשלם כדמים שהיתה בשעת הגזילה, וקאמרי בית הלל כשעת הוצאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:13:2.english: If [it refers] to a decrease - When it decreased in value, where Beit Shammai say he is penalized to pay according to the value it had at the time of the robbery, and Beit Hillel say [he pays] according to [the value at] the time of removal.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:13:3.hebrew: ומי איכא למאן דאמר - היכא דליתיה בעין, דכל הגזלנין לאו כשעת הגזילה משלמין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:13:3.english: And is there anyone who says - where it is no longer extant, that all robbers do not pay according to [the value at] the time of the robbery?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:1:1.hebrew: ומשלם לו דמי כיסי - דמי כשות של קוצים, לפי מה שהשביח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:1:1.english: And he pays him the value of kisei - The value of hops of thorns, according to how much it improved [in value].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:3:1.hebrew: משום דצרורין לא ישתמש בהן - בתמיה. ומה גילוי דעת יש כאן שאין חפץ שישתמש בהם? מאחר שאם הן מותרין קאמרת ישתמש בהן, דהמפקיד אצלו יודע שהוא צריך תדיר למעות, צרורין נמי ישתמש, דדרך כל אדם לצור מעותיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:3:1.english: Because they are bound, he may not use them - [This is asked] in astonishment. And what indication of intent is there here that [the depositor] does not want him to use them? Since if they are loose you say he may use them — because one who deposits [money] with him knows that he constantly needs money — [when they are] bound as well he may use [them], for it is the way of every person to bind his money.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:4:1.hebrew: ואפילו נאנסו - קאמר מתניתין דחייב באחריותן, ואפילו לא נשתמש בהן, דמהשתא הוי שואל עלייהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:4:1.english: And even if they were [lost] due to circumstances beyond his control - The Mishnah is saying that he bears responsibility for them, and even if he did not use them, for from now on he is [considered] a borrower with respect to them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:5:1.hebrew: נאנסו לא - כל זמן שלא נשתמש, לא הוי שואל, אלא אבדו דוקא חייב כשומר שכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:5:1.english: [If] they were [taken by] unavoidable circumstances, [he is] not [liable] - As long as he has not used [the money], he is not a borrower; rather, specifically [if] they were lost, he is liable as a paid bailee.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:5:2.hebrew: ואי שואל לא הוי שומר שכר נמי לא הוי - מה שכר נטל על שמירתם? אלא על שסמך עליהם להחליפן ולהשתכר אם יבא לידו, אתה מחייבו; ושאלה היא זו, שהרי כל הנאה שלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:5:2.english: And if he is not a borrower, he is not a paid bailee either - What fee did he take for guarding them? Rather, [it is] because he relied on them to exchange them and profit if [an opportunity] should come his way [that] you hold him liable; and this is [a case of] borrowing, since all the benefit is his.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:5:3.hebrew: בההיא מודינא - אע"ג דאמינא לא הוי שואל מהשתא עד שישתמש, מודינא דשומר שכר הוי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:5:3.english: In that [case] I concede - Even though I say he is not a borrower from now until he uses [the money], I concede that he is a paid bailee.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:5:4.english: Since he benefits, he provides benefit - to the owner.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:6:1.hebrew: המפקיד מעות - גזבר שהפקיד מעות הקדש, כסבור שהן שלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:6:1.english: One who deposits money - [This refers to] a [Temple] treasurer who deposited consecrated money, thinking that it was his.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:6:2.english: The treasurer has not committed misuse - For [the money changer] did not spend them with permission, and he is not his agent.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:6:3.english: Unbound - For [the depositor] is like one who grants permission, and [the money changer] becomes his agent.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:6:4.hebrew: לפיכך אם הוציא - שולחני, מעל גזבר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:6:4.english: Therefore, if he spent [them] - [i.e.,] the money changer, the treasurer has committed misuse [of consecrated property].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:7:1.hebrew: ואי אמרת אפילו נאנסו - תנא מתני' דחייב שולחני באחריותן, נמצא משעה שהפקידו אצלו יצאו מרשות הקדש ובאו לרשות שולחני, ונעשה כמו שלוה לו, ואין הוצאה גדולה מזו; מאי איריא הוציא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:7:1.english: And if you say [that] even [if] they were lost through unavoidable accident - the Mishnah taught that the money changer is liable for them — it follows that from the moment he deposited them with him, they left the domain of the Temple treasury and entered the domain of the money changer, and it became as though he lent [them] to him, and there is no greater spending than this; why specifically [did it state] "he spent"?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:8:1.hebrew: איידי דתנא רישא הוציא - לאשמועינן רבותא דאפילו הוציא לא מעל, תנא סיפא הוציא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:8:1.english: Since the first clause taught "he spent" - [It did so] to teach us a novelty, that even if he spent [it], he did not commit misuse [of consecrated property]; [therefore,] the latter clause taught "he spent."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:9:1.hebrew: ילקה בחסר וביתר - אם חסרו דמיה, שהוזלה בשוק, ישלם דמיה כמו שהיתה שוה בשעה ששלח בה יד, שהיא שעת הגזילה; וכן כל הגזלנין משלמין כשעת הגזילה. וכגון שהוציאה, שאינה בעין; אבל אם ישנה בעין כמות שגזלה, אומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך", כדאמרינן גבי מטבע ונפסל, תרומה ונטמאת, בפרק הגוזל [קמא] (ב"ק דף צו:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:9:1.english: He is penalized for [its] decrease and [its] increase - If its value decreased, in that it became cheaper in the market, he pays its value according to what it was worth at the time he misappropriated it, which is the time of the robbery; and similarly, all robbers pay [according to] the time of the robbery. And [this applies] in a case where he disposed of it, so that it is no longer intact; however, if it is [still] intact just as he robbed it, he says to him, "Behold, yours is before you," as we say regarding a coin that was disqualified [or] terumah that became impure, in the chapter HaGozel [Kamma] (Bava Kamma 96b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:9:2.hebrew: וביתר - אם שהתה בידו מששלח בה יד ונתייקרה, ואח"כ הוציאה, לוקה ביתר דמיה לשלם כשעת הוצאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:9:2.english: And [for] its increase - If it remained in his possession after he misappropriated it and it increased in value, and afterward he removed it [from his possession], he is penalized for the increase in its value, to pay in accordance with the time of removal.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:9:3.english: And Beit Hillel say, etc. - In the Gemara it explains what [this] means.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:9:4.hebrew: כשעת התביעה - כשעת שיתבעו לדין, ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 43a:9:4.english: In accordance with [its value at] the time of the claim - At the time when he claims it in court, and in the Gemara it explains the reason.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 43a:11:1.hebrew: והתנן כל הגזלנים משלמין כשעת הגזלה - ואע"ג דבפ' הגוזל [קמא] (ב"ק דף צו:) אמרי': "זה הכלל: כל הגזלנים משלמין כשעת הגזלה — לאתויי דרבי אלעאי, דאמר: גנב טלה ונעשה איל, עגל ונעשה שור — נעשה שינוי בידו וקנאה", משמע דלא מיירי ביוקרא וזולא אלא בשינוי, כדמיירי ברישא דמתני': "הגוזל עצים ועשה כלים, צמר ועשה בגדים" — היינו דוקא יתורא ד"זה הכלל", אבל פשטא דמתניתין ד"משלמין כשעת הגזלה" מיירי ביוקרא וזולא. והתם בהגוזל (דף קג.) נמי מייתי לענין יוקרא וזולא גבי אייקר כתנא דרב כהנא, ובפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף לב.) גבי "לפי דמים משלם". וא"ת: רב דאמר במרובה (ב"ק דף סה. ושם ד"ה גופא): "קרן כעין שגנב [כפל וכו']", ואוקמה כגון דמעיקרא שויא ד' ולבסוף שויא זוזא — מאי קמ"ל? מתני' היא! ועוד, מאי בעי התם: "מאי טעמא דרב"? ליבעי מאי טעמא דמתניתין! וי"ל: דרב קמ"ל דאע"ג דקרן כעין שגנב, כפל לא הוי כמו קרן אלא כשעת העמדה בדין; ובעינן מאי טעמא דרב דמחלק כפל מדין קרן, ומשני: "גנבה" ו"חיים" — אחייה לקרן כעין שגנב, דוקא קרן ולא כפל:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 43a:11:1.english: And we learned [in a Mishnah]: All robbers pay in accordance with [the value at] the moment of the robbery - Even though in the chapter [entitled] HaGozel [Kamma] (Bava Kamma 96b) [the Gemara] says [that the phrase] "This is the general rule: all robbers pay in accordance with the moment of the robbery" comes to include [the ruling of] Rabbi Ilai, who said: "[If] one stole a lamb and it became a ram, [or] a calf and it became an ox, a change has occurred in his possession and he acquires it" — [which] implies that it does not speak of appreciation and depreciation, but rather of a physical change, just as the first clause of the Mishnah speaks of: "One who robs wood and makes utensils, [or] wool and makes garments" — that [derivation] is specifically [from] the superfluous phrase "This is the general rule," whereas the plain meaning of the Mishnah, "they pay in accordance with the moment of the robbery," speaks of appreciation and depreciation. And there in [chapter] HaGozel (103a) it also cites [the Mishnah] regarding appreciation and depreciation, in connection with [a case where] it appreciated, like the Tanna of [the school of] Rav Kahana; and in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 32a) regarding "he pays according to monetary value." And if you will say: [Regarding] Rav, who said in [the chapter entitled] Merubbah (Bava Kamma 65a, and see Tosafot there, s.v. "Gufa"): "The principal is [assessed] as at the time he stole [it; double payment, etc.]," and [the Gemara] established it in a case where initially it was worth four [zuz] and at the end it was worth one zuz — what is [Rav] teaching us? It is [already stated in] the Mishnah! Furthermore, what does [the Gemara] ask there: "What is Rav's reason?" Let it ask: "What is the reason of the Mishnah?" And one can answer: Rav teaches us that even though the principal is [assessed] as at the time he stole [it], the double payment is not like the principal, but rather [is assessed] as at the time of standing in court. And [the Gemara] asks what is Rav's reason for distinguishing the double payment from the law of the principal, and answers: "[The verses state] 'theft' and 'living' — revive the principal [to be] as at the time he stole [it], specifically the principal and not the double payment."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 43a:7:1.hebrew: מאי איריא הוציא כי לא הוציא נמי - כיון דהיתר תשמיש מחייב באונסין. וא"ת: הא דתנן לקמן בהזהב (בבא מציעא דף מד. מז: מח.): "נתן לו מעות ולא משך ממנו פירות — יכול לחזור בו", לרב הונא דאית ליה דהיתר תשמיש מחייב באונסין, וכן לרב יוסף בפרק אלו מציאות (לעיל בבא מציעא דף כט.), המוכר אסור להשתמש במעות שקבל; שאם היה מותר להשתמש, תקשה להו הך ברייתא דמייתי אפלוגתא דרבי יוחנן ור"ל: "נתן לבלן — מעל", דוקא בלן דלא מחסרא משיכה, כדקתני סיפא: "הרי מרחץ לפניך, הכנס ורחוץ", אבל ספר — לא מעל עד דמשיך; ולדידהו, כי נתנה לספר נמי למעול אע"ג דלא משיך, כיון דספר מותר להשתמש בהן, בין מיירי בספר נכרי כר' יוחנן, בין בספר ישראל כר"ל. וכמו שאסור להשתמש בהם לרב הונא ולרב יוסף, ה"נ לר"ל ולר' יוחנן, דבהא לא פליגי, ולא הוה המוכר על אותם מעות כי אם שומר חנם לכ"ע. וא"כ, לרבי יוחנן מה הועילו במה שתקנו דאין מעות קונות? דאי מעות קונות, יאמר מוכר: "נשרפו חטיך בעליה"; השתא דלא קני, יאמר: "נשרפו מעותיך בעליה"! ועוד, דרב הונא גופיה סבר בפ' הזהב (לקמן בבא מציעא דף מו:) דבר תורה מעות קונות כרבי יוחנן, דאמר רב הונא: "מכור לי באלו" — קנה. וי"ל: דאע"ג דלא הוי על המעות כי אם שומר חנם, לא מצי א"ל "נשרפו מעותיך בעליה", דכספים אין להם שמירה אלא בקרקע. וא"ת: כיון דהיכא שלא משך אסור להשתמש במעות, א"כ הא דאמר: "פוסק עמו על הגדיש או על שער שבשוק", מה מרויח בהקדמת מעות? וי"ל: כגון שפירש ע"מ להשתמש בהם; א"נ אפילו בסתמ', כיון שהוא פוסק ומקדים לו מעות חצי שנה מן הגדיש עד ימות הקיץ, אדעתא דהכי נותן שישתמש בהן. ועוד י"ל: דלרבי יוחנן ולרב הונא דאית להו דבר תורה מעות קונות, לא הפקיעו כח שיש לו למוכר במעות שיכול להשתמש בהם, כיון דקונות מן התורה, והוי שואל עלייהו ולא מצי א"ל "נשרפו מעותיך בעליה", ולא תקנו משיכה אלא כדי שלא יאמר לו "נשרפו חטיך בעליה". אבל לר"ל ודאי, כיון דמעות אינם קונות, אסור להשתמש במעות ולא הוי שואל עלייהו, ולכך נתנה לספר לא מעל עד שימשוך. וכן לרבי יוחנן ולרב הונא בספר נכרי לא מעל עד שימשוך, דמעות בנכרי אינם קונות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 43a:7:1.english: Why specifically [if he] spent [it]; even [if he] did not spend [it] as well - Since permission to use [the money] renders one liable for unavoidable mishaps. And if you say: Regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah later in [chapter] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 44a, 47b, 48a), "If he gave him money and did not draw [i.e., take physical possession of] the produce from him, he can retract" — according to Rav Huna, who holds that permission to use renders one liable for unavoidable mishaps, and similarly according to Rav Yosef in chapter Eilu Metziot (above, Bava Metzia 29a), the seller is forbidden to use the money he received; for if he were permitted to use [it], that baraita which [the Gemara] cites on the dispute between R. Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish would pose a difficulty to them: "[If a Temple treasurer] gave [sacred money] to a bathhouse attendant, he has committed me'ilah" — specifically a bathhouse attendant, where meshikhah [drawing into possession] is not lacking, as the latter clause teaches, "Behold the bathhouse is before you; enter and bathe," whereas [if he gave it to] a barber, he has not committed me'ilah until he draws [the shears]. Now according to them [Rav Huna and Rav Yosef], when he gave [the money] to the barber he should also commit me'ilah even though he did not perform meshikhah, since the barber is permitted to use them, whether [the baraita] is speaking of a non-Jewish barber according to R. Yoḥanan or a Jewish barber according to Reish Lakish. And just as he is forbidden to use them according to Rav Huna and Rav Yosef, so too [is he forbidden] according to Reish Lakish and R. Yoḥanan, for on this point they do not disagree, and the seller is nothing more than an unpaid guardian over that money according to everyone. And if so, according to R. Yoḥanan, what did [the Sages] accomplish in enacting that money does not acquire? For [the reason for the enactment was that] if money acquires, the seller would say, "Your wheat burned in the attic"; now that [money] does not acquire, he will say, "Your money burned in the attic"! And furthermore, Rav Huna himself holds in chapter HaZahav (below, Bava Metzia 46b) that by Torah law money acquires, like R. Yoḥanan, as Rav Huna said, "[If he said,] 'Sell to me for these [coins],' he acquires [it]." And one can answer: Even though he is nothing more than an unpaid guardian over the money, he cannot say to him, "Your money burned in the attic," because money has no [adequate] safeguarding except in the ground. And if you say: Since where he did not perform meshikhah it is forbidden to use the money, if so, [regarding] that which [it] says, "One may contract with him [for produce] at the [price of the] stack or at the market price," what does [the seller] gain by the advance payment of money? And one can answer: [It is] such as where he explicitly stipulated on condition to use it; alternatively, even without explicit stipulation, since he contracts and advances him money half a year ahead, from [the time of] the stack until the summer, he gives [it] with the intention that he use it. And furthermore, one can answer: According to R. Yoḥanan and Rav Huna, who hold that by Torah law money acquires, [the Sages] did not remove the power that the seller has over the money to be able to use it, since it acquires by Torah law; thus he is a borrower over it and cannot say to him, "Your money burned in the attic," and they only enacted meshikhah so that he would not say to him, "Your wheat burned in the attic." However, according to Reish Lakish, certainly since money does not acquire, it is forbidden to use the money and he is not a borrower over it, and therefore [if he] gave it to a barber, he did not commit me'ilah until he draws [the shears]. And similarly according to R. Yoḥanan and Rav Huna, with a non-Jewish barber he did not commit me'ilah until he draws [the shears], for money does not acquire with a non-Jew.
